notes: Background: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Offering in-app contextual help + search across docs and metrics. Want to introduce an in-product assistant (chat + contextual code snippets) and improve help center search relevance using embeddings + reranking.

Timeline: evaluated hosted API for alpha (internal) in Aug-Sep. Hosted worked well for dev; latency 80-120ms p95 on test corpus. Now negotiating Dedicated for production to meet throughput/SSO/compliance needs.

POC summary (Oct): 2-week POC using hosted endpoints; traffic replay of 500 reqs/s peak, simulating concurrent sessions. Verified generation quality on redwood-verified models (quantized 13b for cheap path, 70b for high-fidelity answers). Key finding: batching + prefix caching reduced token cost ~30% with no user-visible latency impact.
Requirements (customer):
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for chat generation at baseline 200 qps; warm KV-cache expected for session flows
- Throughput: sustained 200 qps with headroom to burst to 500 qps for product launches
- Cost sensitivity: high — want predictable committed pricing and clear overage rules
- Model strategy: prefer default routing to quantized 13- or 34B for most users; automatic fallback to higher-capacity 70B only for long-form/complex answers
- Security: VPC peering + SSO (SAML), audit logs retained 1 year, KMS integration for key wrapping
Pricing negotiation notes:
- Customer asked for 12-month committed capacity (GPU-hours) with quarterly ramp schedule: 30%/30%/20%/20% (months 1-3,4-6,7-9,10-12). Prefer flat monthly invoice vs usage true-up.
- Discussed burst model: customer wants 2x burst allowance per month without overage; after that overage rate to be predictable. They pushed for a soft cap + pay-as-you-go top-up wallet.

- AE (Priya) proposed three tiers: Conserved (low commit), Growth (mid commit + limited burst credit), and Enterprise (high commit + extended burst + SLA). FH prefers Growth with flexibility to move to Enterprise after Q2 metrics review.
- Key negotiation items: volume discount thresholds, definition of 'burst' (sustained for >5 mins counts vs instantaneous), overage pricing per GPU-hour and per-token vs per-minute billing.
Commercial asks from customer:
- Option to convert unused committed hours into credits for the next quarter (no auto-expiry for first year),
- Clear mapping from committed hours -> expected qps for their model mix (13b quantized vs 70b on fallback),
- Attachment to contract: SOW with ramp schedule + migration plan and rollback policy.
Security/compliance conversation:
- They require a DPA and proof of SOC2 type II. Redwood provided SOC2 report and suggested gap plan for their internal auditors.
- KMS design: customer wants customer-managed keys in KMS; asked about HSM support for Dedicated — Redwood engineering flagged Private plan for HSM, but suggested KMS tie-in for Dedicated as interim.
Operational notes:
- SE (Marcus) ran load curves and included recommended config: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline 200 qps on mixed-model routing; +2 GPUs reserved as burst pool (hot spare).
- Suggested autoscaling policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 65-75% with scale-in cool-down of 10m to avoid oscillation during product events.
